messages:
nora: FYI: small operational blip this morning where a policy push caused transient route divergence across a subset of routers. Hedging up ~2% for ~90s. Not a full outage but noticeable.
diego: saw traces. root cause seems twofold: 1) routers accepted snapshot but applied different internal canonical ordering (minor proto ordering diff), 2) we have no quorum check so some routers switched earlier.
sylvie: thinking: introduce a preflight diff+compat check in the policy pipeline that emits a tiny compatibility report and a suggested rollout strategy (grace-window, compatibility-level). That way ops can decide strict vs roll.
rahul: +1. More concrete: when a snapshot is compiled we run three checks: semantic-diff (models/routes changed), capacity-impact-estimate (how many routers likely to flip), and compatibility-class (compatible|degrading|incompatible). Publish results with snapshot metadata.
nora: capacity-impact-estimate? how do we estimate?
rahul: quick heuristic: run a lightweight sim against a rolling sample of recent traffic in the compile cluster. Use decision fingerprints to estimate percent of routers whose local decision would differ. It's probabilistic but cheap.
diego: Nice. Then tie that to a rollout policy: if compatibility-class==compatible && impact<5% -> immediate; if compatible && impact between 5-30% -> staged roll with prefer mode; if degrading/incompatible -> require manual approval and strict canary.
sylvie: also propose snapshot publish handshake: policy-service writes snapshot -> publish "snapshot_ready" -> routers ack receipt -> once quorum (configurable, default 70%) ack we mark snapshot "active". Until active routers should identify themselves as "pre-active" and include that in their decision explainability.
rahul: caveat: ack fanout across regions might be slow. Use region-local quorums for activating per-region strictness. Global active only when a global quorum met, but don't block regional activation for region-local rollout.
nora: ops concerns: adding ack adds complexity. If a snapshot stalls waiting for quorum we need automatic fallback (timeout + auto-activate with softer prefer mode).
diego: agreed. Timeout policy: T_quorum = 10s; if not reached -> auto-activate in prefer mode and emit alert. For strict mode snapshots (explicit tenant requests) require manual override or longer T_quorum.
sylvie: housekeeping: remove volatile fields from snapshot fingerprint (build_ts, ephemeral metadata) and compute canonical_fingerprint.hmac to avoid false mismatches. Also attach compatibility-class and impact_estimate. Routers should use fingerprint+compatibility to decide swap semantics, not raw timestamp.
rahul: metrics to add: policy.preflight.impact_estimate_pct, policy.preflight.compatibility_class, routing.quorum_ack_rate, routing.pre_active_ratio, routing.hedge_delta_post_activate. We'll need Console widgets and an alert if hedges > baseline +1.5% post-activate.
nora: rollout plan: 1) implement canonical_fingerprint + preflight compute in policy-service behind flag (rahul), 2) add publish/ack handshake (diego), 3) router: read fingerprint + prefer logic + pre-active flag (sylvie), 4) telemetry (nora). Test in staging: run mixed-fingerprints and mixed-epoch sims for 24h.
deploy-bot: "policy-service preflight feature flag enabled in staging at 2026-04-15T10:02:22Z"
sylvie: small extra: probes. synthetic probes were amplifying hedges. Add probe-tagging: probes include probe_origin_sig and routers should treat probe-triggered hedges with lower weight for auto-hedge triggers during rollout windows.
rahul: and add an eval step: for any snapshot flagged degrading or incompatible, auto-run the critical prompt-suite and fail the publish if any regression beyond threshold. This avoids surprise semantic regressions.
diego: I'll draft RFC addendum with diagrams: preflight flow, quorum handshake, regional vs global activation, and the timeout semantics. Will include sim config for the impact estimator.
nora: thanks. Please link the RFC to the console dashboards and set an oncall runbook for quorum-failure alerts. Meeting in 30 to review draft. :thumbsup:
